title: Your Nose Can Tell Apart a Trillion Different Smells

scenes.text: Your nose can tell apart at least a trillion different smells.
For almost a century, textbooks said ten thousand. That number came from a nineteen twenty-seven paper with no evidence behind it.
In twenty fourteen, scientists in New York mixed 128 scent molecules into random cocktails and asked people to pick the odd one out.
People could tell two mixtures apart even when they shared over half their ingredients. Do the maths, and that's more than a trillion smells.
Your eyes? A few million colours. Your ears? Around 340 thousand tones.
It works because smell isn't one dial like colour or pitch. Hundreds of receptors fire in combinations, like chords on a piano. What smell takes you straight back to childhood?

description:
Your nose can tell apart at least a trillion different smells.
The old figure of 10,000 traces back to a 1927 paper with no experimental basis. In 2014, researchers at The Rockefeller University, publishing in Science, mixed 128 odour molecules into random cocktails and found people could distinguish mixtures that shared more than half their components. Extrapolated, that means more than a trillion distinguishable smells, far more than the few million colours or roughly 340,000 tones we can tell apart.
What's the one smell that takes you straight back to childhood?
